chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Salih ibn al-Sindi, from Ja'far ibn Basheer, from Ibn Bukayr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It is not befitting for the woman that she aromatises her clothes when she goes out from her house.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman wearing perfume on her clothes when going out in public according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the prohibition of applying perfume to garments with the broader principle of modesty, distinguishing between scent as a personal attribute and its use as a public signal of beauty. This ruling is often interpreted by Shia jurists as a preventive measure against fitnah, ensuring that a woman's presence in public remains dignified and not primarily focused on attracting attention through olfactory allure.
